costGuide.title: Mercedes M276.990 Engine Replacement Cost (UK)
costGuide.labourLine: Fitting a Mercedes M276.990 typically takes 12-16 hours at £65/hr (independent specialist rate) - confirm exact labour when comparing quotes, as the 90-degree V6 "hot-vee" turbo layout requires careful access planning.
paragraphs: The final cost of a Mercedes M276.990 engine replacement is heavily influenced by the condition of the twin turbochargers and the timing chain guides. Biturbo variants carry a premium due to the complexity of the hot-vee turbo plumbing and intercoolers. Additionally, direct-injection variants often require intake valve carbon cleaning during the swap. failures.title: Mercedes M276.990 Engine Problems - What Actually Fails

items.title: Timing Chain Stretch and Guide Wear
items.whatHappens: The M276 family is susceptible to timing chain stretch and plastic guide wear over time. This manifests as a distinct metallic rattling noise on cold starts, followed by check engine lights indicating camshaft correlation faults. If ignored, the chain can jump teeth, leading to catastrophic valve-to-piston contact.
items.repairVsReplace: If caught early, replacing the timing chain kit, tensioners, and guides is viable, though it is a labour-intensive job requiring significant front-end strip-down. If internal damage has already occurred, a full Mercedes M276.990 engine replacement is the only reliable solution.

items.title: Camshaft Position Sensor and Wastegate Rattle
items.whatHappens: The camshaft position sensors on the M276 can begin to fail, triggering warning lights and drivability issues. Additionally, the twin turbochargers are prone to wastegate actuator wear and linkage rattle, leading to boost pressure faults and underboost complaints.
items.repairVsReplace: Sensor replacement is a relatively straightforward fix. However, if wastegate rattle progresses to bearing wear and oil ingestion, the turbochargers must be replaced, which can push the requirement toward a fully rebuilt unit if internal scoring has occurred.

variants.title: How to Confirm You Have the Mercedes M276.990
variants.intro: The M276.990 engine code is stamped directly onto a machined pad on the engine block, typically located near the oil filter housing or the bell housing. It is also clearly listed on your vehicle's V5C registration document under "Engine Number" and can be decoded from the full VIN. Common Confusion Warning: Owners frequently confuse the M276.990 with other variants in the M276 family: - M276.920: The 3.0L V6 biturbo variant. While similar, it has different displacement, turbo sizing, and ECU calibration. - M276.940: The 3.5L naturally aspirated variant. It lacks the twin-turbo setup entirely, making the intake and exhaust architectures completely incompatible. - M276.960: The 3.5L biturbo variant found in SUV applications (like the GLE400). While mechanically similar, the M276.990 is tuned specifically for sedan/coupe applications with different engine mounts, exhaust routing, and ECU software. Fitting the wrong revision will result in severe ECU, wiring loom, and exhaust manifold incompatibilities.

buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement Mercedes M276.990 - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: A used Mercedes M276.990 is only advisable for lower-mileage host vehicles and *only* if accompanied by documented, stamped service history proving the timing chain and guides have been inspected or replaced. Without this history, the risk of inheriting the same catastrophic chain-jump issues is unacceptably high.

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: This is the most recommended route for the M276.990. A proper reconditioned unit will include brand-new timing chain components, refreshed valve cover and oil cooler gaskets, and tested twin turbochargers, directly addressing the engine's known weak points out of the box.

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: A full rebuild is justified if your original M276.990 suffered a jumped timing chain that damaged the cylinder head, valves, or pistons, or if turbo bearing wear caused oil starvation to the crankshaft. A specialist rebuild will machine the block, fit updated timing components, and ensure all oil galleries are clear of debris.

buyingGuide.supplyFitLine: Sourcing a replacement is only half the job. Our network provides full supply and fit services, ensuring the engine is installed by Mercedes-specialist technicians with a nationwide warranty backing both the labour and the unit.
buyingGuide.vehicleValueNote: For flagship hosts like the W222 S-Class and C218/C257 CLS, current UK market values typically sit between £10,000 and £35,000 . With a reconditioned M276.990 replacement costing from £3,800 (plus fitting), the repair cost generally represents 20-40% of the vehicle's value, making replacement financially viable and a safe investment for well-maintained examples.

items.question: What is the most common failure with the Mercedes M276.990 engine?
items.answer: The most documented failure patterns for the M276.990 are timing chain stretch/guide wear and turbo wastegate rattle or camshaft position sensor wear. Early warning signs include a metallic rattle on cold starts, camshaft correlation fault codes, or boost pressure faults, and if the chain jumps teeth or turbo bearing wear leads to oil ingestion, a full engine replacement is required.

This includes the S-Class (W222) and the CLS (C218/C257), and you should always verify your exact fitment via registration lookup before ordering parts.

items.question: Should I buy a used or reconditioned Mercedes M276.990 engine?
items.answer: A reconditioned Mercedes M276.990 is strongly recommended over a used unit due to the well-documented timing chain and turbocharger failure risks. Used units carry a high probability of inheriting the same latent wear unless accompanied by stamped proof of a full chain kit replacement, whereas a proper reconditioned M276.990 includes new timing chain components, refreshed gaskets, and tested twin turbochargers as standard.

items.question: What is the difference between the M276.990 and other M276 sub-codes?
items.answer: The M276.990 is the 3.5L biturbo variant tuned specifically for sedan and coupe applications like the S-Class and CLS. The M276.920 is a 3.0L biturbo, the M276.940 is naturally aspirated, and the M276.960 is a 3.5L biturbo tuned for SUVs, meaning fitting the wrong variant will result in severe ECU, wiring loom, engine mount, and exhaust manifold incompatibilities.
